tasks.short: Use handtools, instruments and powered workshop equipment safely

steps.what: Select and use handtools, gauges, power tools, jacks and hoists safely

tasks.design: Keep tool selection, positioning and physical operation with the mechanic. Existing workshop instructions may be read from {DOCS}, but this task provides no separate document-production step to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires physical access, force control, safe positioning and situational awareness.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital maintenance records do not operate workshop tools or make the work physically disappear.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unstable loads, damaged tools and unsafe working positions.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic feels, hears and sees conditions and stops the operation when needed.
tasks.altitude: Tool-operation time and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a safe tool and work area under mechanic direction
reach.learn: Load safety and stopping when uncertain

evidence.claim: Digital job cards alone do not reduce the physical labour of using workshop tools; this is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is physical tool use, excluding repair-log entry, purchasing and invoicing.
Mechanic checks tool condition and job instructions during the retained operation; no structured safety approval is assumed and no automated action consumes one.
Existing powered tools and lifting equipment are today's means and earn no new software saving. Check native instructions before any future custom reference work.
No software or process is introduced; upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Tool mix and local authorisation requirements
research_questions: Is any separate repeated preparation step present that can be measured without reducing safe tool use?

already_counted.description: Safe selection and physical tool operation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and difficult operations retain physical and safety time; existing equipment runtime earns no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect and test defective equipment to diagnose malfunctions

steps.what: Inspect, test and listen to defective equipment using suitable instruments
Diagnose malfunctions by comparing symptoms, measurements and possible causes

tasks.design: Retain hands-on inspection, measurements and diagnostic reasoning, using the existing diagnostic instrument {OTHER}. A fault code is evidence to interpret alongside physical findings; it does not automatically establish the failed component.
tasks.previous_blocker: Intermittent faults and interacting causes require tests in actual equipment conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital job-card capabilities establish no replacement for these physical tests and interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing root causes from secondary symptoms without unsafe or unnecessary dismantling.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic can change the test when sounds, access conditions or inconsistent measurements contradict a first hypothesis.
tasks.altitude: No change to diagnostic time or responsibility.

reach.task: Compare a recurring vehicle symptom with test evidence

evidence.claim: Physical measurements and professional fault diagnosis are not replaced by digital maintenance logging; this is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is inspection, testing and diagnosis, excluding repair execution and later job-card transcription.
Mechanic produces symptoms and measurements in s1 before using them in s2. Test instruments are {OTHER}; no complete structured defect code or automatic root-cause label is assumed.
Existing instrument acquisition time and functions are baseline and earn no new saving. Check native instrument and reference facilities before later custom work.
No new system or process is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Vehicle mix and current diagnostic instruments
research_questions: Which diagnostic delays come from source retrieval rather than essential testing or reasoning?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Both routine and intermittent defects retain inspection and interpretation time; no paperwork baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and repair vehicle heating and cooling systems

steps.what: Locate the correct heating and cooling technical procedure for the vehicle
Diagnose heating and cooling faults through inspection and measurement
Repair heating and cooling components and verify correct operation

tasks.design: Configure vehicle and system filters over current technical manuals in {DOCS}. The mechanic verifies applicability, diagnoses with existing test equipment {OTHER}, repairs components and retains all physical checks and functional testing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right variant-specific procedure can take repeated manual searching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source indexing can shorten lookup without suggesting an unverified repair.
tasks.still_hard: Safe access, intermittent faults, contamination and confirming the repair actually works.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic can detect conditions that make a nominally correct procedure unsuitable.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less manual hunting; diagnosis and physical repair time are unchanged.

reach.task: Locate a requested current manual for mechanic checking
reach.learn: Vehicle variant identification and source version control

evidence.claim: Indexed technical manuals may shorten variant-specific lookup while physical diagnosis and repair remain; this is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary includes procedure retrieval, diagnosis and physical repair, excluding general repair-log drafting and vehicle release certification.

Mechanic captures vehicle identifier, model variant, system type, manual revision and procedure selection within s1's 7 retained hours. No ready structured fault classification is assumed; uncertain variants require manual lookup.
Test native manual search before custom indexing. Existing reference shortcuts earn no new gain. Diagnostic instruments are {OTHER} and do not decide the repair.
Local qualifications and safe-work requirements still apply; no automatic equipment control is introduced. Overlap with general diagnosis must be allocated once in a role roll-up.
unknowns: Manual access, variant data and retrieval burden
research_questions: Can a manual index shorten lookup without selecting the wrong vehicle variant or outdated procedure?

already_counted.description: Vehicle identification, field capture and applicability checks

incremental.description: Maintain technical source links and revision information

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=7+35+55=97; gross 3 minus 1 upkeep gives net 2. High assumes repeated manual searching; low removes only 1 hour, offset by upkeep. Diagnosis, repair and testing retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Follow water, energy and waste conservation practices

steps.what: Follow green operational practices for water, energy and solid waste

tasks.design: Retain the mechanic's physical conservation and waste-handling actions. Existing instructions can remain in {DOCS}; the task does not establish a separate reporting or metering process that earns labour savings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conservation depends on equipment use, physical segregation and habits in a changing workshop.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital records alone do not perform the required physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Separating contaminated material correctly and noticing avoidable resource use during work.
tasks.human_edge: The mechanic recognises local exceptions and can stop an unsafe disposal or wasteful operation.
tasks.altitude: No reduction in conservation duties or physical handling time.

reach.task: Resolve an unsuitable workshop waste or resource-use arrangement
reach.learn: Practical conservation and safe disposal requirements

evidence.claim: Conservation actions remain physical work unless a specific equipment or process change is established; this design introduces none.

assumptions: Boundary is following conservation practices, not creating environmental reports or installing metering infrastructure.
Mechanic observes conditions and acts within s1. No structured waste code, meter feed or automatic conservation status is assumed.
Existing facilities and instructions are baseline. Review native facility controls before future custom software; this design makes no equipment changes.
No service is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Current conservation instructions and disposal facilities
research_questions: Which physical facility change would reduce resource use without creating unsafe handling?

already_counted.description: Physical conservation and safe waste handling

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0. Routine and exceptional conservation actions retain their physical time; environmental benefit is not mislabelled as labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce a small amount of technical-manual retrieval while retaining hands-on tool use, diagnosis, repair and conservation work.
reach: Help maintenance helpers identify correct technical sources and supervisors resolve practical workshop exceptions
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic with reliable technical references who remains responsible for physical testing, safe repair and practical resource conservation.
